one_liner: Threads API is a free REST Graph-style API with OAuth 2.0 user tokens; self-serve dev access works for testers, but multi-user use needs Meta App Review.
auth_notes: Authorization-code flow at threads.com/oauth/authorize; short-lived (1h) tokens exchanged for 60-day long-lived tokens, refreshable. App access tokens (client_credentials) exist only for narrow APIs like oEmbed.
access_notes: API is free and self-serve for app roles/testers (own account), but users without a role on the app require per-permission Meta App Review (and Tech Provider verification per some sources).
blocker_notes: Meta App Review required per permission before arbitrary end users can authorize the app; development and testing possible meanwhile with tester accounts.

evidence.quote: API authentication is handled by Threads user access tokens that conform to the OAuth 2.0 protocol.
Use an app access token to make requests to the Threads API on behalf of an app rather than a user.
Posting to your own account needs a Meta app and no review. Posting for other people needs App Review
Meta publishes no paid tier, no per-call fee, and no pricing page in the official Threads developer docs.
Use the `GET /{threads-user-id}?fields=id,username,...` endpoint to return profile information about a Threads user.
Unofficial MCP server for Meta's Threads API. Enables LLMs like Claude to publish posts, manage replies, and track insights through the Model Context Protocol.
